newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Israel may invest in Bulgaria tourism, arms plants.
newsitem.headline: Israel may invest in Bulgaria tourism, arms plants.

text.p: Israeli companies are interested in investing in Bulgaria's tourism, arms and food industries, ambassador David Koen said on Tuesday.
"Israeli businessmen are interested in acquiring small hotels in Bulgarian mountain resorts that would cater to our tourists who visit this country," Koen told a news conference.
"We are also interested in investing in Bulgarian arms plants and in helping them overhaul their production to reach NATO standards," he added.
Bulgaria has lifted a privatisation ban on some of its 90-odd plants producing military equipment.
The two countries plan to start talks on setting up a free trade zone in September, and finalise an accords on avoiding double taxation and agricultural cooperation, said Koen.
Turnover between the two countries fell last year by some 40 percent to $39.5 million from $68 million in 1995, Bulgaria's deputy trade minister Mincho Gerdjikov told the same news conference.

Bulgaria's exports to Israel amounted to $30.5 million last year, mainly in chemicals, metals, farm produce and food. Israel's exports to Bulgaria were $9 million, mostly in machines and mineral products.
The decline was attributed mainly to Bulgaria's economic crisis.
Direct Israeli investment in Bulgaria totalled $600,000, said Gerdzhikov.
"We have many ideas and we will begin implementing them once a stable government and parliament are in place," said Koen.
General elections are scheduled for April 19.
